decisions.reason: The coolant pressure booster extends the firm's core coolant management offer, is promoted publicly and carries invested development effort, so dropping it after one year would write off that investment without results that rule out temporary causes.
The cleaning centrifuge fits the announced direction toward sustainable coolant filtration and has sunk engineering cost, so management will persist and attribute any early weakness to ramp-up.
Coolant nozzles are a low-investment add-on, but they complement the coolant systems the firm has committed to and cost little to keep listed, so withdrawal is unlikely.
Scraper belt chip conveyors are central to the firm's established chip conveying business and are publicly listed, so there is no reason to abandon them.
The magnetic belt conveyor builds on the core conveyor line, which the firm has visibly committed to, and its modular range makes keeping it the default.
Hinged belt chip conveyors are a staple of the firm's identity in metalworking material flow, so dropping them would contradict its strategy and earlier commitments.
